items_missed: No agenda statement at all — never told the customer what the call would cover or roughly how long, and never asked 'sound good?'
Never asked 'How are you today?' ('How can I help you today?' is not the same beat).

Availability was never actually confirmed. She asked for the date 'so I can check the availability' but never came back with an answer for the 25th — and the customer's specific request for a later-in-the-day slot ('our building is kind of busy during morning') went completely unanswered.
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no closing sense-check.
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) or the 60c/lb baseline — only listed 'insurance' inside the included-items run-on.

No booking attempt. The customer deferred to talk to her partner before the rep ever asked for the schedule; the 'no deposit is required' line came after the deferral as an afterthought rather than as a close.
Never asked 'Any other questions before I let you go?'
Email handoff incomplete — no bolded-details-at-top mention, no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask, no business hours.
Never asked about packing services or moving stressors.

No sense-check after the pricing block — the customer had to ask three clarifying questions in a row ('is that the total?', 'what is the hourly rate?', 'so no other flat hourly charge?') to unpack it.
Never used the customer's name once — 'ma'am' throughout, and referred to her as 'Hannah' at one point.
top_strength: The estimate section was the strongest of the three calls graded — she used the school-bus equivalent to get a walk-distance answer out of a customer who couldn't measure it, gave a typical 2.5-3.5 hour range for a one-bedroom, then explained exactly why this one lands at the 2.5 hour minimum (same building, elevator access, no drive time, no traffic to absorb). The customer's response was 'that makes sense, that's really cool.'
coaching_note: Jeline's discovery and estimate reasoning are strong; the front and back of the call are where she's losing points. Open with a real agenda statement and close by actually asking for the booking — she gave a clean $510 quote and then let the customer walk to 'I'll discuss it with my partner' without ever asking for the schedule. Also: she left the customer's one explicit constraint (a non-morning slot) unanswered for the whole call.
phone_presence_notes: Warm-sounding language ('definitely ma'am,' 'no worries ma'am,' 'of course ma'am') and the customer stayed comfortable, but the warmth is formulaic rather than personal — zero name use, and the customer's stated morning-traffic concern got acknowledged with a 'thank you' and never addressed.
